name: Spinach Beet
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth and goosefoot family
grown_as: Perpetual spinach: a leaf beet with thin green stalks, picked like spinach over a long season. William's records give no variety.
habit: An upright rosette 30 to 50 cm tall and 30 to 40 cm across from a thick crown on a tough taproot. A biennial: in the second year a leafy, branched flowering stem 1 to 1.2 m.

leaf.outline: Oval to slightly triangular, 10 to 20 cm long
leaf.base: Broadly wedge-shaped to rounded, running a little way down the stalk
leaf.veins: A narrow pale green midrib about 5 mm wide; side veins few and curving
leaf.stalk: Long, slender and green, about as long as the blade, slightly flattened

flower.form: Tiny green star-shaped flowers without petals, in clusters along long thin spikes
flower.petals: None: five small green tepals, curved inwards
flower.centre: Five short stamens with yellow anthers round a low green centre
flower.behind: A small narrow green bract under each cluster
flower.carried: Stalkless in clusters of two or three, spaced along long, slender, leafy spikes that branch from a tall stem; the spikes arch and droop at the tips
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: The flowers in each cluster fuse as they ripen into a hard, corky, knobbly 'seed' (a seed ball) 3 to 5 mm across, light brown, holding two to four true seeds. One seed ball sown gives a clump of seedlings.
seedling: Seedlings come up in little clumps from each seed ball. Two narrow strap-shaped glossy seed leaves, often on a reddish stem, then oval true leaves on green stalks.
winter: Usually lasts through winter as a smaller rosette and crops again in spring before it flowers.

leaf: an oval glossy blade with smooth edges
a slender green stalk about as long as the blade
a narrow pale midrib, not the broad one of chard
bloom: tiny green flowers with no petals
stalkless in small clusters along a thin spike
seed: a knobbly corky brown seed ball 3 to 5 mm
young: an upright rosette of oval glossy leaves on green stalks
no stem, leaves from the crown
crop: a rosette of many oval glossy leaves on slender green stalks
flower: a tall leafy stem branching into long thin arching spikes
seedhead: long spikes crowded with brown knobbly seed balls

look_alikes: Spinach has narrow seed leaves too but a softer, darker leaf and bolts in its first summer. Swiss chard has broad coloured stalks and midribs.
